title: CHAPTER 3: OFFICIAL LANGUAGE POLICY IN BANKS

blocks.content: 3.1 RBI Rajbhasha Policy and Annual Programme

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issues an Annual Programme setting progressive targets for Hindi usage across banks.
Town Official Language Implementation Committees (TOLIC) monitor policy implementation at the city level through bi-annual review meetings.
Banks observe Hindi Week and Hindi Month around September 14 to encourage adoption through competitions and awareness drives.
Standard Hindi training programmes for bank personnel include Prabodh, Praveen, and Pragya courses.
Incentive schemes offer cash awards, honorariums, and increments for bank employees conducting original work in Hindi.

blocks.content: Reserve Bank of India issues Annual Programme for Official Language Implementation each year in accordance with the Annual Programme issued by the Government of India (Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs). Banks are required to comply with targets set in this programme.

cells: RBI issues guidelines to banks under Sections 21 and 35A of Banking Regulation Act, 1949; also under Official Languages Act 1963 and Rules 1976
Department of Official Language (DoOL) issues annual programme with targets for each quarter; banks must achieve these targets
Banks submit QPR to DoOL and RBI on implementation; format prescribed; TOLIC (Town Official Language Implementation Committee) coordinates
Banks must increase percentage of correspondence, noting, communication, cheques, forms, etc. in Hindi each year
All forms, passbooks, account statements, cheque books, FD receipts must be in bilingual (Hindi and English) format
Banks must ensure their core banking software (CBS), mobile banking apps, ATM screens are available in Hindi; Unicode-based Hindi enabled on all systems
Every bank's Annual Report must contain a chapter on Official Language implementation; reviewed by Parliamentary Committee
Banks must arrange Hindi training (Prabodh, Praveen, Pragya) for all staff; track and report training completion
Town Official Language Implementation Committee (TOLIC) :नगर राजभाषा कार्यान्वयन समिति
Formed at town/city level; comprises all Central Government offices in that town; bank branches and offices are included
Senior-most officer of an identified Central Government office in the town; rotates generally
Coordinate and oversee Official Language implementation among member offices; share best practices; review progress
Quarterly meetings; review progress; discuss problems; share strategies
Member offices inspect each other (peer inspection); send inspection report to TOLIC; TOLIC inspects member offices in turn
Give awards for best Hindi implementation; publish house journal; organise Hindi week / Hindi month
TOLIC submits half-yearly report to Regional Implementation Office of DoOL

rows: Employees with mother tongue other than Hindi / basic knowledge
Employees who have passed Prabodh or equivalent
Employees who have passed Praveen or equivalent

cells: Commemorates adoption of Hindi as official language on 14 September 1949 by Constituent Assembly; national holiday for Hindi commemoration; awards given by Home Minister
Month-long programme of Hindi promotion; essay competitions, debates, dictation, translation contests, seminars; encouraged in all Central Government offices
Similar to Hindi Month but shorter; some departments observe 1–14 September
Week-long celebrations; Hindi competitions; felicitation of employees doing excellent Hindi work
Commemorates first World Hindi Conference held in Nagpur on 10 January 1975; Indian missions abroad celebrate; international Hindi promotion

blocks.content: 3.4 Hindi Training Programmes for Bank Employees

items: Questions frequently test the minimum meeting frequency for TOLIC (held twice a year).
Sequence and target group for Hindi courses: Prabodh (beginner), Praveen (intermediate), and Pragya (advanced).
Regional categorization rules under Rajbhasha Policy (Region A, Region B, and Region C targets) are heavily tested in Banking Rajbhasha Officer exams.

cells: Basic level :learn to read and write Hindi; for those with no Hindi knowledge
Non-Hindi speaking staff; Region C/B employees without Hindi background
Intermediate level :read, write, and do correspondence in Hindi; pass Praveen exam
Employees who have completed Prabodh or have basic Hindi knowledge
Advanced level :proficiency in translation, noting, drafting in Hindi; highest level
Senior staff; those wanting proficiency for official Hindi work
Typing in Hindi on computers; Unicode Hindi; Devanagari keyboard
Clerical and assistant staff who need to type in Hindi
Hindi correspondence, noting, drafting for bank-specific work; banking terminology in Hindi
All bank employees; mandatory for Region A and B staff within defined timelines

blocks.content: 3.5 Incentive Scheme for Hindi Work in Banks

cells: Employees doing original noting/drafting in Hindi (not translation) get monetary incentive as per bank's scheme aligned to DoOL guidelines
Cash prizes for winners of in-house Hindi competitions; encouraged during Hindi Month
Employees who pass Prabodh, Praveen, Pragya exams receive lump-sum incentive payments; reimbursement of exam fees
Employees can claim reimbursement for purchasing approved Hindi books; encourages Hindi reading
Best performing office in TOLIC gets annual Rajbhasha Shield; individual employees get certificates
Home Minister's award to Central Government offices doing excellent Hindi work; different categories (A, B, C Region); banks compete
Given by Home Ministry to individuals, committees, institutions; for Hindi promotion; cash award
